Dnešní kapacita = kolik si dnes můžete d: Today’s capacity = how much you can afford today. Two kinds of limits keep it. PLAN: this week (Monday to Sunday) stays within its target in the cycle (90 / 100 / 110 / 55 %). SAFETY: (1) the unabsorbed load of the last days doesn’t exceed your weekly capacity — the same one the Load tab shows (capacity + 15 % margin, by the week’s readiness); older days count only in part, by how much of them the body has already absorbed, (2) no single run goes past your single-run capacity. Total load (heart rate × time from all activities, including movement outside training above your usual day) has its own target and ceiling and is converted into kilometres and minutes in Z4+. The strictest limit applies — each channel shows which one, and its tag says whether it is the plan or safety. When only the plan is met and the safety limits have room, a short optional recovery run or an easy ride stays available at a readiness of at least 80 %. When mechanics is over its threshold of 25, today shrinks further (volume −20 %, intensity and descent halved); when load is over its threshold, a recovery week follows.
Kolik zátěže bude zítra k dispozici podl: How much load tomorrow will have room for, depending on what you still do today and how you sleep. It uses the same rules as today’s capacity: today’s load is absorbed only in part overnight (muscles, tendons and bone on a fixed half-life of 3.5 nights, heart and lungs by the morning’s readiness: faster after a good night, slower after a weaker one), the weekly ceiling moves with the 7-day average readiness and the single-run ceiling with tomorrow’s readiness. The week’s target drops by what you do today; when tomorrow is a Monday, next week’s target in the cycle applies. It is an estimate — in the morning the real night from your watch, new pain or a check-in refine it.
Kumulativní zátěž kalendářního týdne (od: The calendar week’s cumulative load (from Monday) day by day, split by where it came from: running, other sport, strength and movement outside training above your usual day (that one counts in total load only). The dashed line is the week’s target in the cycle, the dashed block above today is how much you may still do today. A hatched block above it appears when only the plan is met: that much more the safety limits would allow. Below the chart is what the week’s target (plan) and the weekly ceiling (safety) are made of — your proven weekly capacity, the week’s readiness and the margin.
Skóre stavu (0–100): čím vyšší, tím lépe: Status score (0–100): the higher, the better. It is 100 minus a risk made up of mechanics, load and symptoms, weighted by the strength of the evidence. 100 = nothing to watch. Above 60 is low risk, 31 to 60 watch, 30 and below high risk. When a safety rule, recurring pain or the load state moves the day into a higher band, its place in the band follows their severity together with the model. On ordinary days the display brings out even small differences. Each signal shows how many points it takes off the score. The letter A, B or C at a signal is the strength of the research evidence: A strong, B moderate, C weaker or indirect. Always against your own history.
